summary.headline: Honasa Q1 FY27: revenue grew 32% with EBITDA near INR110 crore and PAT INR90 crore; management says FY27 growth will beat the high-teens five-year CAGR.
summary.overview: Management reported 32% growth, EBITDA of almost INR110 crore, PAT of INR90 crore, and about INR83 crore of cash generation, with 30.5% volume growth. Management attributed margin expansion to B2B mix, A&P efficiency, opex leverage (about 100 bps) and a non-recurring one-time opex benefit, and said the one-time item was not recurring. Focus categories grew 35%+ and reached about 85% of sales; Mamaearth accelerated to high-teens growth and the second INR1,000 crore brand (The Derma Co.) was announced. Management also disclosed the entry into fragrances (FIKN) and the Fluence Pharma acquisition under Honasa Health, still pending conditions precedent.

segments.name: Mamaearth
segments.commentary: Accelerated to high-teens growth in Q1 FY27, driven by focus categories; Rice face wash is now the number one face wash, Rosemary shampoo above INR100 crore ARR, and both online and offline grew at strong double digits.

segments.name: The Derma Co.
segments.commentary: Now the second INR1,000 crore brand in the portfolio and has entered the teens EBITDA club; latest contribution about 80% online and 20% offline (GT plus MT), with presence in close to 50,000 GT outlets.

segments.name: BTM Ventures (acquired January 2026)
segments.commentary: ARR of INR150 crore in the latest quarter, grown almost 100% since acquisition; expanded to Maharashtra, opened a new category and new channels.

segments.name: Young brands (Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt, Staze, Reginald)
segments.commentary: Growing 30%+ excluding BTM Ventures; Aqualogica relaunched in Q1 targeting Gen Z; Reginald expanding on two marketplaces and into new geographies; specific ARR not disclosed.

segments.name: Fragrances (FIKN) and Honasa Health
segments.commentary: FIKN launched as India's first elixir-based fragrance brand, clinically tested for 12-hour stay; Honasa Health subsidiary formed for nutrition and wellness, with the Fluence Pharma acquisition still in conditions precedent and diligence.

guidance_outlook: Five-year plan: high-teens revenue CAGR and EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps a year to reach 15% EBITDA margin in five years; FY27 expected to beat this CAGR and expand margin by at least 150-200 bps.
Mamaearth expected to deliver double-digit CAGR over five years and to grow better than planned CAGR this year.
Q2 expected to see sequential dip in scale as summer seasonality fades; management said growth-first mindset means reinvestment where needed.
Reported and like-to-like growth expected to converge from Q2 once the Flipkart settlement base is clean; this is the last quarter of the settlement slide.
Packaging and crude-linked cost inflation expected to hit from Q2; calibrated price increases taken at end of Q1 to offset it.
capex_capacity: Honasa Health subsidiary created for nutrition and wellness; Fluence Pharma acquisition pending condition precedent and diligence completion.
The Derma Co. has offline presence in close to 50,000 GT outlets; company tracks reach of about INR3 lakh outlets per AC Nielsen universe, driven mainly by Mamaearth.
Distribution: direct distribution narrowed to focus on 100 cities; distributor inventory tracked and distributor inventory under 30 days.
Q1 cash generation of about INR83 crore with negative working capital; collections at highest levels.
demand_pricing: Market share gains: about 350 bps in face wash and 160 bps in shampoo in modern trade/offline (per management).
Quick commerce share gains tracked at category level via platform data; management says branded search share is higher on quick commerce than e-commerce.
Fragrance penetration in India 3% vs 11% globally; management sees fragrance as a horizon-two category.
Gen Z cited as ~45% of buying cohort in B2C categories, mainly e-commerce.
Packaging price index rising; company says price increases taken late Q1 to offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth expectation for the rest of the year, and how does Mamaearth trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated high-teens five-year CAGR and said FY27 will be better than that CAGR, with Mamaearth also ahead of its planned double-digit CAGR this year; no quantified guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion is organic versus seasonal, and does seasonality reverse from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 should see at least 150-200 bps of margin expansion, with a clearly above-average year; the seasonal benefit is expected to fade from Q2 as summer categories normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company about no repeat of past distributor inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is extremely confident: distributor inventories are tracked, collections are at highest ever levels, and distributor inventory is under 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Derma Co. split between online and offline, and where is it in offline scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Derma Co. revenue is about 80% online and 20% offline (GT plus MT), with GT presence in close to 50,000 outlets; offline effort is about a year old.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't fragrance been cracked by large Indian players, and what was the learning from the earlier Mamaearth fragrance experiment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier Mamaearth fragrance extension was shut down because consumer PMF was poor; it argued fragrance needs to be a fragrance-first brand, and built internal R&D over about two years before launching FIKN.

qa_highlights.question: How has the company offset packaging and crude-linked cost inflation in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory management protected Q1 gross margin; the real impact is expected from Q2, which calibrated price increases taken at end of Q1 are expected to offset.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA guidance too conservative given Q2 seasonality and H2 patterns?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 ex one-time was about 12% margin; Q2 scale dips sequentially and the company remains growth-first, reinvesting where needed; margin target remains 100-150 bps a year over four to five years.
